items.title: Professor Longhair (Henry Roeland Byrd) Interview, 1969-05-30
items.q: cause a brother Montgomery was a friend of mine

ctx.x: That's why I picked a little hype. You know, the bands at the land of the air. And all the schools used to go to the matinees.

Yeah. And until we sat down one day, we said we're going to make some real money. We're going to get a band. We did. We got out of Bama. Big Bama. We played trumpet. That's his father Tux I was telling you about. He was his piano player. And Charlie up here would drink so much. His brother Junior was on the drums. We had no bass player at that time. And when everything was over with, that music just stayed in me. For some reason I knew around and I drift back to Junior's drums. One night Junior was sick and I had…

I learned the boogie woogie. I learned the boogie woogie. I said, songs are this easy to play. I can put them together myself. First, second, and third change. I know it ain't before balls. Distant measurement. And all, so. I said, you think I can learn music? I said, by the time you learn music, you'd be too old to play. Go in on and play. It's playing, you know. And if you get lucky enough to learn music in between, you got it made. But I had always been told that whether you could play or not, you could read,…
